Bug-fix release: every bug report filed since 0.17.1. Several are security fixes, so upgrade soon.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Sandboxed scripts now need Landlock** (Linux 5.13 or later; Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+ and the Docker image all have it). On a host without it, sandboxed scripts refuse to run until you set `DANBYTE_SCRIPT_SANDBOX=none`, which runs them unconfined and says so in every run log.

> [!NOTE]
> **Behaviour changes:**
> - API tokens can only be created, listed or deleted from a signed-in session, not with another token.
> - External secret paths on device credentials are deployment-admin only, and never reach into a tenant's own folder.
> - Spreadsheet import matches rows in their own scope (prefixes and IPs by VRF; VLANs, racks and locations by site), refuses ambiguous names, and validates like the API. Cables can only be updated by import, not created.
> - Engine, SNMP and VRF picks on the site, location and device edit forms are saved with the form's Save button.
> - Topology opens grouped by site on tenants with more than 500 devices, unless you have picked a grouping.

### Security

- #315 - **Vault and Azure secret paths stay inside the tenant's own folder.** A tenant could read or overwrite another tenant's managed secrets through a crafted credential path.
- #316 - **Sandboxed scripts are confined with Landlock.** They can no longer read the worker's environment, `.env` or other files in the install, or reach Redis and the database directly.
- #317 - **Editing a trusted script's code clears its trust**, and only the owner or a `trust` holder can make a script run as its owner or widen its token.
- #318 - **API tokens are managed from a signed-in session only.** A token, including a script's run token, could create permanent tokens, also for another tenant.
- #320 - **Removing an authenticator needs the password or a current code**, a TOTP code works once, and an account that must use two-factor enrols at sign-in instead of skipping it.
- #321 - **Outbound requests to virtualization sources and the assistant are pinned to the checked address and refuse redirects**, closing a way around the SSRF guard.
- #322 - **A set-password or invite link no longer re-enables a disabled account.**
- #323 - **The presence socket checks view permission on the object**, as the presence API does.
- #326 - **The assistant call log masks secrets at every level** of a write payload; stored entries are masked on upgrade.
- #327 - **Assistant search respects the allowed object types.**
- #328 - **Assistant batch requests count every call toward the rate limit**, with a body and batch size cap.

### Data

- #309 - **Clean images are stored exactly as uploaded**, and animated GIFs and WebPs keep their frames; `strip_photo_metadata` no longer loses frames or originals.
- #324 - **Opening a site's edit form no longer resets its monitoring engine.**
- #330 - **Re-importing an unchanged spreadsheet no longer moves objects** to another device, prefix or rack; imported devices get their components and the rack overlap check.
- #331 - **IP lookups stay in their VRF** when a prefix creates its gateway and when SNMP attaches an observed address.
- #333 - **Modules own the interfaces they install**: removing, replacing or deleting a module's bay acts on exactly those interfaces, and sync no longer deletes them.
- #334 - **Front-port ranges map to consecutive rear positions**, a front port must map to its own device's rear port, rear ports can't drop used positions, and trace follows the strand through MPO ports.
- #335 - **Name ranges keep zero padding** (`Eth[01-04]`) and `[5-5]` expands instead of being stored literally.
- #348 - **Import validates custom fields** like the API.
- #349 - **Import ignores `numid`**, which is export-only.
- #350 - **Bulk update validates values like a single edit**: bad values get a 400 and nothing is written.
- #351 - **Import applies the API's rules** for VLAN ranges, rack locations and cables.
- #352 - **An import row without an id no longer overwrites another site's VLAN, rack or location.**
- #353 - **Import dry run reports the same errors as the real import**, in plain words.
- #354 - **Empty lists survive an export and re-import**; fields an earlier re-import emptied are repaired, and the custom field edit page no longer crashes on them.
- #355 - **Tags export again**, and tag names with `;` or without a tenant round-trip.
- #356 - **Long-stable checks keep their history after the nightly prune**; checks already affected are repaired on upgrade.
- #357 - **Webhooks and auto-deploy wait for the change to commit**, so rolled-back changes send nothing.
- #361 - **Upgrades and `bootstrap` keep your status defaults and availability**; types that got a second default are repaired.
- #310 - **A DIN rail can't be shortened under a device being mounted at the same moment.**
- #311 - **Device type bundle import applies the device type checks.**
- #312 - **The site map counts a multi-port cable's links by position**, not once per pair of ports.
- #329 - **Rack power from PDU ratings uses the smaller side** of a redundant pair.

### Monitoring and notifications

- #325 - **Outposts poll every device bound to them**, including devices bound directly or by the tenant default; the SNMP card says where polls run from.
- #347 - **Stacked switches no longer report name drift** on members other than the master.
- #358 - **Notification channels treat HTTP errors as failures**: Send test reports them and status changes are retried.
- #359 - **A status change is sent once**, even when two workers pick it up together.
- #360 - **A scheduled backup is retried when the job queue was down**, and one failing schedule no longer stops the others.

### Performance

- #337 - **The prefix list is fast at any size** (a page of 50 at 5,000 prefixes: 16 s to 0.14 s).
- #339 - **The IP list uses an index** for its default order.
- #340 - **The MAC address list** no longer runs extra queries per row.
- #341 - **The circuit list** no longer runs an extra query per row.
- #342 - **The change log is fast for users with site-limited grants.**
- #343 - **Grouped topology is computed from counts** (5.5 s to 0.3 s on 3,200 devices), and large tenants open grouped by site.
- #362 - **`assign_numids` works in short batches** and no longer blocks new objects while it runs.

### Upgrades

- #346 - **The upgrade disk-space check shows how it adds up**, and the installation guide lists the minimum requirements.
- #363 - **Processes still running the old code keep working** right after the migrations, until they restart.
- Editing a user no longer emails them a password-reset link unless you tick the box.

Thank you @deku-m, @SerhiiZahuba and @jorge-madrigal for the detailed reports.
